## Tidepool landing page build plan

**1. Header**  
A slim horizontal bar: Tidepool wordmark on the left, “How it works,” “For teams,” and “Pricing” centered, with “Sign in” and a solid “Try Tidepool” button on the right. Use warm white, ink-blue text, and a small aqua brand mark. Keep the type clean and sans-serif.

**2. Hero**  
Use a two-column layout: headline, supporting copy, and paired calls to action on the left; a crisp product screenshot on the right. Show a weekly planning board with teammate avatars, movable task cards, and a shared “This week” column—not a vertical timeline. Headline: **“Make a week your whole team can get behind.”** Supporting copy: “Bring priorities, owners, and plans into one calm space. Adjust together as the week changes.” Buttons: “Start planning free” and “See a sample week.” Add a small note: “No credit card required.”

**3. Trust strip**  
A narrow band below the hero with a short line—“Built for small teams that do their best work together”—and a row of understated customer logos or team-name placeholders. Use muted slate on pale blue-gray; keep this section quieter than the hero.

**4. Benefits**  
Three equal cards with simple geometric illustrations: “See the week at a glance,” “Know who owns what,” and “Make changes without the scramble.” Pair each with one sentence focused on a practical outcome. Use soft aqua, lavender, and butter-yellow accents against white cards.

**5. How it works**  
A two-column section with a larger interface crop on the left and three numbered steps on the right: “Set the focus,” “Share the work,” “Adapt together.” Explain the flow in direct, specific language; highlight the active step with a colored number badge.

**6. Team scenario**  
A full-width pale-lavender panel showing a sample Monday-to-Friday plan for a small product team. Use realistic task names and owners to demonstrate how planning works in context. Caption: “A clear plan, even when priorities shift.”

**7. Final CTA**  
Center a concise invitation on a deep navy background with a subtle, abstract overlapping-circle motif. Copy: “Give next week a better starting point.” Button: “Plan your first week.”

**8. Footer**  
Simple, compact links for product, company, and help, plus copyright and privacy links. Use warm white and subdued blue-gray text.

## Tidepool landing page build plan

**1. Header**  
A clean horizontal nav: Tidepool wordmark left, “How it works,” “For teams,” and “Pricing” in the middle, “Sign in” and a filled “Try Tidepool” button right. Use warm off-white, ink text, and a small sea-glass mark. Keep the navigation compact so the product remains the focus.

**2. Hero**  
Two columns: direct, benefit-led copy on the left; a large, legible product preview on the right. Show a shared Monday–Friday planning board with priorities, owners, and a few visible changes—not a decorative dashboard. Headline: **“Make a plan your team can actually use.”** Supporting copy: “Bring the week’s priorities, owners, and moving parts together—so everyone knows what matters next.” Primary CTA: “Plan your week free”; secondary: “Explore a sample week.” Add “Free to start. No credit card required.” Use ink-blue type, sea-glass accents, and a small marigold highlight on the board.

**3. Credibility strip**  
A restrained band beneath the hero: “For small teams who need a clearer week, not another meeting.” Follow with verified customer logos if available; otherwise use a concrete product reassurance such as “Made for teams of 3–30.” Avoid unverified testimonials or logo placeholders.

**4. The problem and payoff**  
A split section: concise copy on the left, three illustrated moments on the right—priorities scattered, ownership unclear, plans changed. Resolve each with a short benefit: “One shared view,” “Clear owners,” “Room to adjust.” Use simple, friendly line illustrations with soft sand, aqua, and lilac fills.

**5. Product in action**  
Show a larger, close-up board screenshot, annotated with small numbered labels: “Set priorities,” “Assign an owner,” “Update the plan.” Keep callouts outside the interface so the product stays readable. Copy should explain what teams do, not promise effortless transformation.

**6. A week, made visible**  
Full-width pale-aqua panel with a realistic sample team plan across five columns. Include a midweek priority change to show how the plan adapts. Caption: **“A shared plan that can change without getting lost.”**

**7. Final CTA**  
Centered on deep ink-blue, with a subtle sea-glass ripple pattern. Headline: “Start next week on the same page.” Button: “Build your first plan.”

**8. Footer**  
Compact product, company, and help links; privacy and terms. Keep the warm-white background and muted ink typography.
